items.q: Define relative atomic mass.
items.a: The ratio of the average mass of one atom of an element to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. It has no unit.

Define atomicity.
items.a: The number of atoms present in one molecule of an element or compound. Example: O₂ is diatomic, O₃ triatomic, P₄ tetratomic.

items.a: Moles of water = 0.18 ÷ 18 = 0.01 mol. Molecules = 0.01 × 6.023 × 10²³ = 6.023 × 10²¹ molecules.

items.q: Calculate the number of moles in (i) 27 g of Al (ii) 1.51 × 10²³ molecules of NH₄Cl.
Give the salient features of modern atomic theory.
items.a: 1) An atom is no longer indivisible; it is made of protons, neutrons and electrons. 2) Atoms of the same element can have different masses (isotopes, e.g. ₁₇Cl³⁵ and ₁₇Cl³⁷). 3) Atoms of different elements can have the same mass (isobars, e.g. ₁₈Ar⁴⁰ and ₂₀Ca⁴⁰). 4) Atoms of one element can be changed into another by transmutation. 5) Atoms may not combine in simple whole-number ratios (e.g. sucrose C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁). 6) The mass of an atom can be converted into energy (E = mc²). 7) The atom is the smallest particle that takes part in a chemical reaction.

items.q: Derive the relationship between relative molecular mass and vapour density.
items.a: Vapour density = mass of a volume of gas ÷ mass of the same volume of hydrogen. By Avogadro's law equal volumes have equal numbers of molecules, so VD = mass of 1 molecule of gas ÷ mass of 1 molecule of H₂ = mass of 1 molecule ÷ (2 × mass of 1 H atom). Relative molecular mass = mass of 1 molecule ÷ mass of 1 H atom. Therefore 2 × vapour density = relative molecular mass.

items.x: The idea of the atom was first proposed by Greek philosophers in the fifth century BC (BCE); it was more philosophical than scientific.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a postulate of the modern atomic theory?
o: Atoms of the same element may have different atomic masses
Atoms of one element can be transmuted into atoms of another
The mass of an atom can be converted into energy
An atom is indivisible and indestructible
items.x: Modern atomic theory says the atom is no longer indivisible (electron, proton, neutron discovered) and no longer indestructible (artificial transmutation).

items.q: The existence of 18Ar40 and 20Ca40 supports which postulate of modern atomic theory?
o: Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios
Atom is the smallest particle in a chemical reaction
Atoms of the same element may have different masses
Atoms of different elements may have the same atomic mass
items.x: Ar-40 and Ca-40 are isobars: atoms of different elements with the same atomic mass.

items.q: Glucose (C6H12O6) and sucrose (C12H22O11) are cited in modern atomic theory to show that:
o: Atoms can be converted into energy
Atoms of the same element can have different masses
Atoms may not always combine in a simple whole-number ratio

items.q: The mass number of an atom is the sum of its:
items.x: The mass of an atom comes mainly from protons and neutrons, so their sum is called the mass number.

items.q: One atomic mass unit (amu) is defined as:
o: One-sixteenth of the mass of an oxygen-16 atom
The mass of one hydrogen atom
One-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom
items.x: Atomic mass unit is one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, which has 6 protons and 6 neutrons.

items.q: In the modern system, the symbol 'amu' has been replaced by:
items.x: The chapter notes that 'amu' is no longer used; the symbol 'U' denotes unified atomic mass.

items.q: Arrange the standards used for measuring relative atomic mass in the order they were adopted:
items.x: Hydrogen was the first standard, later replaced by oxygen, and now carbon-12 is used.

items.q: Relative atomic mass is otherwise called:

items.q: Which modern method of determining atomic mass uses C-12 as the standard?

items.q: Consider the statements: 1. Relative atomic mass has no unit. 2. Atomic mass expressed in grams is called gram atomic mass. Which is/are correct?
items.x: Relative atomic mass is only a ratio, so it has no unit; expressed in grams it is called gram atomic mass.

items.q: Why is the atomic mass of carbon given in the periodic table as 12.01 amu and not 12.00 amu?

items.x: Periodic-table masses are average atomic masses; carbon's is the weighted average of C-12 (98.90 %) and C-13 (1.10 %).
